cells.tense: Right now, the direction is yours to set and you are here for it.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Choose a small habit to grow this week — water it daily, read what it asks for, and change the aim when it tells you.
cells.core:
You can aim at something and hold the line, and you can redraw the line when the ground shifts. You push when the thing needs pushing. You let go when it's finished rather than when you're tired, because the two feel different to you and you know which is which.

What's free to grow next is care that doesn't spend you. Choose a small habit to grow — water it daily, read what it asks for — and change the aim when it tells you the aim should move. Nothing has to be forced for it to keep going. What you're steering gets more like itself, and so do you.
cells.sheetLine: You can change course without abandoning what you decided to steer.
cells.place: at the point where direction is chosen and kept

cells.tense: Ahead of you, an outcome is being defended that has not arrived yet.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Sort what you're bracing over into plain facts on a page, leaving mood outside, and follow what the page says.
cells.core:
Going well, this is plain: you set a direction, the outcome is allowed to arrive when it arrives, and you meet what shows up rather than what you feared. There's room between deciding and knowing how it lands. You can hold a plan without gripping it, and the day stays yours while you wait.

The future is being settled before it has happened. Something ahead looks like it must land a certain way, and the whole day gets arranged around a version of events that hasn't shown up. From outside it reads as certainty; from inside it is bracing. Contact with what's actually here is what's thin, not resolve. Sort what you're bracing over into plain facts on a page, leaving mood outside, and follow what the page says rather than what the waiting says.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing at a future you can't write in yet.

cells.tense: There was a direction you meant to take, and you have not picked it up again.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Lay one step you can already see, solidly, then set it down and don't plan the next.
cells.core:
Going well, this is simple: you point yourself at something, the direction holds, and the days get laid under it the way slabs get laid under a wall — one at a time, each one true before the next. You can feel the weight of a plan without holding all of it at once. That's the shape you know.

The pointing has gone quiet. Decisions sit open, the days pass without a direction being picked, and the first step is still waiting there, unlaid. It isn't refusal. It's an IOU you haven't had to pay. Strength returns through building, not through wanting harder: lay one step you can already see, solidly, then set it down and don't plan the next.
cells.sheetLine: The direction you meant to take is still waiting where you left it.
cells.place: at the point where direction is chosen and kept

cells.tense: The direction is already being chosen, and you would say it is anyone's doing but yours.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Bring fresh hands to what you're keeping going — put down what you expect it to need and see what it asks for.
cells.core:
Directing is already happening — a routine kept, something held together, hours pointed somewhere — and your account of it stops short of the part where you chose. As you'd put it, the day decides and you show up. Anyone who has watched you keep something steady would not describe you as a passenger in it.

Start where growth actually starts: with what's in your care. Bring fresh hands to what you're keeping going — put down what you expect it to need and see what it asks for. What you already set in motion gets a place to be seen, by you first.
cells.sheetLine: You are already steering, and you say the day is doing it.
cells.place: at the point where direction is chosen and kept
